<Rep. Bennie G. Thompson>: H. Res. 114 directs the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to provide the Committee on Homeland Security any information in its possession related to the security implications of halting disbursement of DHS grant funds. In January, the President barred departments and agencies from awarding congressionally authorized and funded Federal grants, creating chaos throughout the Federal Government and among grantees. As directed by Congress, DHS administers a range of grants--including for disaster response, terrorism prevention, and first responders--primarily to State and local governments. Given the important role DHS grants play in the security and resilience of communities across the country, it is critical that the Committee understand whether and what analysis DHS performed regarding how freezing grant funds would affect national preparedness, disaster response, and first responders prior to implementing the President's grant freeze.
One of the most chaotic days of the second Trump presidency was January 27, when the White House issued a careless and sloppy memo telling Federal agencies to stop providing Federal grant funding to State and local governments across the country. The memo was so bad that courts had to intervene to prevent it from taking effect, and after publicly defending it, the White House rescinded the memo.\1\
\1\Melissa Quinn, Richard Escobedo, & Kristin Brown, Trump administration rescinds federal funding freeze memo after chaos, CBS NEWS, Jan. 29, 2025, https://www.cbsnews.com/news/trump-funding-freeze-rescinded-memo/.
Even with court intervention and the White House attempting to rescind the memo, there are still reports that Federal grants are being withheld from our communities.
H. Res. 114 demands transparency on the impact of blocking critical DHS grants, which directly threatens national security by cutting vital funding for first responders, disaster recovery, and community safety programs--creating chaos and undermining our preparedness. For example, DHS's Transit Security Grant Program is the primary means through which the Federal Government provides security support to mass transit, passenger rail, ferries, and bus systems. Trump's attempted grants freeze--combined with his tearing down of key transportation advisory committees and firing of TSA and FAA employees--puts our transportation systems at greater risk, even as we experience a shocking increase in transportation accidents.
This Committee needs to know who from DHS thought it was a good idea to jeopardize this funding and their rationale and research, if any, on the implications of doing so. Because right now, none of that has been shared with the Committee or the public.
Donald Trump's decision to block congressionally authorized Federal grants has halted crucial funding for programs like the Urban Area Security Initiative, the State Homeland Security Program, the Nonprofit Security Grant Program, the State and Local Cybersecurity Grant Program--each vital for emergency response, terrorism prevention, and law enforcement support. Chaotic disruptions of grant funds leave the boots on the ground in a lurch, undermine the goals of the grant programs, and attack national security.
Republicans who doubt the impact of the grant funding freeze memo would do well to reach out to their State and local governments and first responders and ask them about the impact of Donald Trump's threat to take away DHS funding.
The grant funding freeze means that State and local governments and first responders may not get reimbursed for the millions they have already spent to protect and support our communities--dollars promised to them by the Federal Government. At a minimum, the payments will be delayed--and communities cannot afford to go months or years without being paid back due to a disorganized and shoddy memo from Donald Trump--nor should they have to.
The DHS grants that are under threat by the Trump administration are ones that this Committee has supported in a bipartisan fashion for years. Every Member of Congress should be alarmed that--with a push of a button, without even a conversation or letter to Congress--the Trump administration is undermining support for first responders back home.
Democrats on this Committee are committed to safeguarding national security, but regrettably, by adversely reporting H. Res. 114, Committee Republicans have stopped our efforts to conduct effective oversight of the Trump administration's chaotic disruptions of grant funds.
Bennie G. Thompson.
